reviews.text: Robert Rodriguez’ ... forked tongue-in-cheek From Dusk Till Dawn [is] a blast, replete with Peter Cushing in-joke and a disco ball of burning death.
reviews.author: Stephen A. Russell

reviews.text: It’s two films in one: a ruthless crime picture out of the Tarantino playbook that takes a detour to a Mexican brothel that turns out to be a nest of bloodsuckers ...
reviews.author: Sean Axmaker

reviews.text: From Dusk Till Dawn has stylish direction coaxing its genre-bending narrative, with bouts of dark hilarity, all centered by the charismatic George Clooney. This vampire jaunt has a one-of-a-kind bite.
reviews.author: Kristy Strouse

reviews.text: Despite all the talent involved, it's fair to say that this 1996 film is regarded as a cult favorite rather than a classic.
reviews.author: Alistair Lawrence

reviews.text: The story is about the Gecko brothers, Clooney as Seth and Tarantino as Richie, two exceedingly dangerous bank robbers who are on a maniacal crime spree. The ultra-violent movie is pitch-perfect in its stylistic mayhem.
reviews.author: Michael Calleri

reviews.text: What an inexplicably bizarre, frequently ugly, intermittently nonsensical, confused experiment of a movie.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: Filmmaker Robert Rodriguez, working from Tarantino's screenplay, opens From Dusk Till Dawn with an electrifying pre-credits sequence revolving around a robbery gone horribly wrong...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: "From Dusk Till Dawn" answers the question about George Clooney, but raises a couple about Quentin Tarantino.
reviews.author: Jay Carr

reviews.text: [Robert] Rodriguez pushes the envelope but fails to make any lasting impression except revulsion at the spectacle of acclaimed independent filmmakers wasting their talents on such trash.
reviews.author: David Hunter

reviews.text: Still sizzles like a capsaicin-spiked grindhouse meatloaf baked and served just under the wire of its sell-by date.
reviews.author: Nick Rogers

reviews.text: This is the "Reservoir Dogs" with a twist of "Near Dark" set to the tune of "Assault on Precinct 13."
reviews.author: Felix Vasquez Jr.

reviews.text: Based on an early Tarantino script, Rodriguez' movie is an incoherent B-pic, in which the sensibilities of the two filmmakers clash.
reviews.author: Emanuel Levy

reviews.text: It is a shame to see so much good talent giving such low-yield results.
reviews.author: Steve Biodrowski

reviews.text: Energetic low-budget vampire nonsense from Robert Rodriguez and Quentin Tarantino.
Imagine two movies plucked from opposite sides of the video store.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: A deliriously trashy, exuberantly vulgar, lavishly appointed exploitation picture, this weird combo of road-kill movie and martial-arts vampire gorefest is made to order for the stimulation of teenage boys.
reviews.author: Todd McCarthy

reviews.text: On a mindless exploitation level this is pretty good, but on other levels it seems to make promises that it fails to deliver on.
reviews.author: Jonathan Rosenbaum

reviews.text: A tired, humorless pastiche of various exploitation genres that is not the least bit imaginative in its campy deconstruction of conventions.
reviews.author: Hal Hinson

reviews.text: Nihilistic and initally unpleasant ... Once the vampires appear (unfortunately about 60 minutes too late), the movie becomes uproarious entertaiment with the most intense humans vs. vampires showdown since 1985's Fright Night.
reviews.author: Chuck O'Leary

reviews.text: Like a Cheesecake Blizzard: It's a pulpy mess loaded with empty calories, but it's so divine that once you start, you can't help but shovel it into your mouth until the last drop, brain freeze and diet be damned.
reviews.author: Phil Villarreal

reviews.text: These guys were going for a B-movie feel, lots of blood, lots of guts, lots of tits and ass, and lots of fun, and for the most part, they achieved their goals.
reviews.author: JoBlo

reviews.text: This is a B-movie, albeit a largish budget B-movie, but with an undeniable B-movie spirit.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Mr. Rodriguez demonstrates his talents more clearly than ever -- he's visually inventive, quick-witted and a fabulous editor -- while still hampering himself with sophomoric material.
reviews.author: Janet Maslin

reviews.text: Ask yourself "am I the kind of person who finds topless vampire strippers a source of constant amusement?" Only those who answer an enthusiastic "YES!" need apply.
reviews.author: Rob Vaux

reviews.text: I can think of worse things to sit through than an orgy of bullets, exploding corpses, and stripper vampires.
reviews.author: Brian Mckay

reviews.text: This film is 'exploitation' in more than one sense of the word.
reviews.author: Dragan Antulov

reviews.text: A weird double-bill in itself: Part one's a crime drama, part two vampire splatter flick. It's an awkward pairing, but there's fun to be had.
reviews.author: Luke Y. Thompson

reviews.text: The picture shows what happens when a writer (Tarantino) and a director (Rodriguez) come together and reinforce each other's worst tendencies and misconceptions.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: A drop-dead-erotic scene a seduction dance by the bar's featured performer, Santanico Pandemonium ... is one of the two reasons to see this movie.
reviews.author: Kim Williamson

reviews.text: For those with a twisted sense of humor, it is entertaining.
reviews.author: Leslie Rigoulot

reviews.text: The characters were as empty as the story.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: This movie is just too much fun not to like.
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: From Dusk Till Dawn is an hilarious piece of genre filmmaking.
reviews.author: Ryan Cracknell

reviews.text: The sickest, most perverted movie within memory. Guiltily, I liked it. But what the hell is it?
reviews.author: Joe Baltake

reviews.text: It's clever, brash and -- if you're into it -- entertaining movie-making that has it all ways, allowing you a stylishly cynical noninvestment, alongside an old-fashioned attachment to the regular guy.
reviews.author: Cynthia Fuchs

reviews.text: From Dusk Till Dawn will be a real disappointment for most Tarantino fans.
reviews.author: Mark R. Leeper

reviews.text: The way-over-the-top campiness is so completely ridiculous, it's impossible to take anything in the film seriously. And trust me, that's not a bad thing.
reviews.author: Christopher Null

reviews.text: It's great fun, but certainly not great art.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: This is horror with a wink and a nod to drive-in theatres and sweaty back seats. This is how it's done.
reviews.author: Marc Savlov

reviews.text: As the bloodsuckers attack our 'heroes' again and again, you feel like you're watching a video game -- from dusk to dawn.
reviews.author: Andy Seiler

reviews.text: From Dusk Till Dawn was probably spawned from an all night bender during which Tarantino and Rodriguez thought it would be fun to see if they could make a deliberately lame movie with someone else's money.
reviews.author: Rob Blackwelder

reviews.text: The movie, which treats you with contempt for even watching it, is a monument to its own lack of imagination.
reviews.author: Desson Thomson

reviews.text: Fans of the genre will like it, especially in the no-holds barred second half. Others are advised to avoid this one.
reviews.author: Madeleine Williams

reviews.text: What we have here in From Dusk Till Dawn is Pulp Fiction with teeth.
reviews.author: Liz Braun

reviews.text: I don't mean to dismiss his films, which I enjoy, or cast aspersions on his character, but I've got to admit -- when Tarantino plays his own sordid parts, he gives me the creeps.
reviews.author: Bryant Frazer

reviews.text: The film is so flamboyantly gory and disgusting, so vulgar and in-your-face obnoxious, with so many offensive subplots and wacked-out elements that you may give up long before you need to reach for your second headache tablet.
reviews.author: Chris Hicks

reviews.text: A fun, tongue-in-cheek gorefest that both spoofs and celebrates the glories of B-grade exploitation vehicles.
reviews.author: Michael Dequina

reviews.text: The filmmakers' references, their winks and nods to the audience, are far more diverting than the picture itself.
reviews.author: Walter V. Addiego

synopsis: On the run from a bank robbery that left several police officers dead, Seth Gecko (George Clooney) and his paranoid, loose-cannon brother, Richard (Quentin Tarantino), hightail it to the Mexican border. Kidnapping preacher Jacob Fuller (Harvey Keitel) and his kids, the criminals sneak across the border in the family's RV and hole up in a topless bar. Unfortunately, the bar also happens to be home base for a gang of vampires, and the brothers and their hostages have to fight their way out.
